articles.title: Trump bought Nvidia shares, then cleared path for chip sales to China: Report
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump bought millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares before taking decisions that eased restrictions on the chipmaker's exports to
articles.body: US President Donald Trump bought millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares before taking decisions that eased restrictions on the chipmaker's exports to China, an analysis of his financial disclosures has found.According to an analysis by anti-corruption group DeKleptocracy, Trump's disclosures show he purchased between $1 million and $5 million worth of Nvidia stock in the days before his administration scrapped a Biden-era export rule in May 2025.The rule, known as the diffusion rule, was intended to restrict exports of advanced US-made artificial intelligence (AI) chips to China over concerns that Beijing could use the technology to develop superior AI capabilities. Its removal opened the way for Nvidia to expand sales in a market that accounted for about a quarter of its revenue between 2010 and 2022.Nvidia shares rose in value after Trump announced the reversal. His disclosures also showed purchases of shares in other technology companies, including Apple, Meta and Microsoft.The president's Nvidia investments continued as his administration moved to ease restrictions further. In December 2025, Trump announced that Nvidia would be allowed to sell its H200 chips to China. The US commerce department approved the move in January 2026.The decision drew criticism over the potential implications for US national security. Experts said the H200 chips were among Nvidia's most advanced products and were six times more powerful than the chips available in China at the time, the Guardian reported.The council on foreign relations warned that their sale could “supercharge” China's future AI factories and strengthen the US's rival.Trump's financial disclosures indicate that he made at least three Nvidia stock purchases in the days after announcing the H200 decision. Each transaction was valued between $250,001 and $500,000. He appears to have made dozens of Nvidia-related stock transactions since taking office, with some ranking among his largest purchases.The stock purchases have come amid separate scrutiny of Nvidia's links to an alleged Chinese intelligence operation. Reports have alleged that Alice Huang, described as a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang, and that her company, Megaspeed, obtained billions of dollars' worth of the chipmaker's products.Trump was briefed twice by US intelligence officials on their assessment that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset, but did not act on it, according to The Guardian.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Anthropic IPO to test Wall Street's faith in AI as skepticism mounts
articles.summary: Anthropic seeks a valuation of approximately $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion.
articles.body:
There were no rockets decking Wall Street bank lobbies this past week, unlike the spectacle surrounding SpaceX's blockbuster June listing.

Instead, bankers marketing Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) potentially record-breaking initial public offering this week faced an unusually turbulent backdrop as Treasury yields surged and a widespread Microsoft Outlook outage hampered communications, all during — the biggest disruption of all — the sudden ousting of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is among Anthropic's biggest investors and chip suppliers.

At a JPMorgan Chase investor event Friday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei outlined a future in which AI could help make diseases such as cancer and Alzheimer's relics of the past, while devising entirely new markets in scientific research, robotics, and cybersecurity.

"We can have a much more beautiful world ... It sounds starry-eyed. It sounds crazy. I really do believe it," Amodei told JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon.

Yet Amodei struck a more restrained tone about the company's move to go public, saying he hopes the company will "underpromise and overdeliver."

"We're not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day or what market conditions we go public into," he added.

The comments come as Anthropic seeks a valuation of approximately $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion, below the $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion figures investors had contemplated just weeks earlier.

The offering, expected to begin trading on Thursday, Nov. 19, could provide one of the clearest tests yet of investors' appetite for AI at a moment when enthusiasm for the broader trade is showing signs of cracks.

The contrast between Anthropic's lofty ambitions and Amodei's measured approach to the IPO has also been apparent in Wall Street's marketing campaign.

The lobbies of JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, and Goldman Sachs have been decorated to welcome the startup, according to people familiar with the arrangements. But the displays are more subdued than the digital displays and skyscraper illuminations of rocket ships Wall Street bank visitors witnessed during SpaceX's June IPO, or the meteorite exhibit at JPMorgan's Manhattan headquarters.

Banks are nevertheless mounting a substantial effort to attract investors.

At Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the two banks leading the offering, Anthropic executives met with institutional investors earlier this week. Goldman is also planning an event next week for wealth management clients, where the bank's president, John Waldron, is expected to interview Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and CFO Krishna Rao, according to a people familiar with the plans.
